package handlers

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
)

// ReadinessCheck verifies required runtime dependencies.
type ReadinessCheck func(ctx context.Context) error

// HealthHandler serves liveness and readiness endpoints.
type HealthHandler struct {
	Ready        ReadinessCheck
	Capabilities map[string]string
	// ReadinessFailureCode maps known failures to static, bounded codes.
	// It must never return dependency error text or private runtime data.
	ReadinessFailureCode func(error) string
}

// Healthz reports process liveness.
func (handler HealthHandler) Healthz(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
	writeStatus(w, http.StatusOK, "ok")
}

// Readyz reports whether required dependencies are available.
func (handler HealthHandler) Readyz(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if handler.Ready == nil {
		writeStatus(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "not ready")
		return
	}
	if err := handler.Ready(r.Context()); err != nil {
		var failure map[string]string
		if handler.ReadinessFailureCode != nil {
			if code := handler.ReadinessFailureCode(err); code != "" {
				failure = map[string]string{"error_code": code}
			}
		}
		writeStatusWithCapabilities(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "not ready", failure)
		return
	}
	writeStatusWithCapabilities(w, http.StatusOK, "ready", handler.Capabilities)
}

func writeStatus(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, value string) {
	writeStatusWithCapabilities(w, status, value, nil)
}

func writeStatusWithCapabilities(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, value string, capabilities map[string]string) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	body := map[string]string{"status": value}
	for key, capability := range capabilities {
		body[key] = capability
	}
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(body)
}
